decisions.quote: This study was a replication and extension trial of our original study examining the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of a brief guided self-help treatment for binge eating disorders in a nonspecialty health care (HMO) setting ( 23 , 39 ).
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and the blind coder classify the paper as a replication. The authors conduct a new randomized clinical trial in an HMO sample to re-test the findings of their earlier CBT-GSH effectiveness trial (ref. 23).

corrected_value.title: Cognitive behavioral guided self-help for the treatment of recurrent binge eating.
corrected_value.authors: Striegel-Moore RH, Wilson GT, Debar L, et al.

decisions.quote: In summary, this study replicated and extended the findings from our earlier study ( 23 ), which demonstrated that a CBT-GSH intervention could significantly improve clinical outcomes for binge eating in a highly cost-effective manner ( 39 ).
decisions.reason: Shipped row 55 misidentified Reference 1 (Hudson et al., 2007, 10.1016/j.biopsych.2006.03.040, an epidemiological study cited only as background context whose title contains 'National Comorbidity Survey Replication') as the original study. The actual original trial re-tested and directly compared in Table 2 is Reference 23 (Striegel-Moore et al., 2010, 10.1037/a0018915), matching blind target 0.

decisions.quote: Replication of the pattern of previous findings suggests that CBT-GSH is a robust treatment for patients with recurrent binge eating. The magnitude of changes was significantly smaller than in the original study, however, suggesting that patients recruited and assessed with less intensive procedures may respond differently from their counterparts enrolled in trials requiring more comprehensive procedures.
decisions.reason: Once original identity is resolved to Striegel-Moore et al. (2010) (ref. 23, blind target 0), both the shipped record and the blind coder agree the replication outcome is successful. The authors state an explicit affirmative overall replication verdict in both the Abstract and Discussion/Conclusions; per the codebook, a lower raw abstinence rate does not make the outcome mixed when the authors conclude the intervention effect replicated with even larger effect sizes vs. usual care.

decisions.quote: This study was a replication and extension trial of our original study examining the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of a brief guided self-help treatment for binge eating disorders in a nonspecialty health care (HMO) setting ( 23 , 39 ).
decisions.reason: Blind target 0 (Striegel-Moore et al., 2010, 10.1037/a0018915) was unmatched only because shipped row 55 had a wrong original citation (Hudson et al., 2007). Because row 55 is paired with target 0 via the original-identity correction on row 55, target 0 is already accounted for and is not an omitted row.

decisions.quote: In summary, this study replicated and extended the findings from our earlier study ( 23 ), which demonstrated that a CBT-GSH intervention could significantly improve clinical outcomes for binge eating in a highly cost-effective manner ( 39 ).
decisions.reason: Reference 39 (Lynch et al., 2010, 10.1037/a0018982) is the companion economic analysis of the same original trial (Reference 23). While the present study re-tests the clinical effectiveness outcomes from Reference 23 (Table 2) and reports descriptive health service and medication utilization counts (Table 3), it conducts no cost or cost-effectiveness analysis and does not re-test Reference 39's cost-effectiveness findings. Thus Reference 39 is not a separate omitted replication target.
